chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about as-salam (advance payment for goods), and it is as-salf (advance payment) regarding silk and the goods which are made in the city in which you are. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, if it is for a known term.'

key_terms.أَجَلٍ مَعْلُومٍ: Ajal ma'lum: A known, specified term or deadline for delivery.
key_terms.السَّلَف: Salaf: Advance payment or pre-payment in a trade context.
key_terms.السَّلَم: Salam: A contract of sale where the buyer pays in advance for goods to be delivered later.
key_terms.الْمَتَاع: Al-mata': Goods, merchandise, or items of trade.

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for the validity of advance payment (salam) in Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi, transmitted through the chain of Samaanah, validates the 'salam' contract in silk and local manufactured goods, a practice widely used in pre-modern Shia commercial jurisprudence to mitigate risk in agriculture and trade. The condition of a 'known term' (ajal ma'lum) ensures certainty (gharar) is removed, aligning with the principles of *fiqh al-mu'amalat* as elaborated by later scholars like Al-Shaykh al-Mufid and Al-Tusi.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at who said,

‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the submission of the advance payment, and it is the retainer regarding the silk and the goods which are made in the city which you are in’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, when it was to a known term’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from Sama‘ah who has said the following: “

I once asked him (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about advance payment to receive goods on a date in future which is payment in advance for silk or goods made in the location where you live. He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, it is lawful if the time is known.’”
